text:
Maya Chen: heads up — seeing a flurry of ALB target removals in us-west-2 after a GPU nodegroup scale-up. health checks failing, targets marked unhealthy and deregistered. anyone watching? :eyes:
Jared Kahn: same. noticed a bunch of 502/504s from the alb logs around the scale event. looks correlated with a spike in pod restarts and readiness not passing.
Lin Wei: can you paste a sample ALB log line? also which target type (ip/instance) for the edge TG?
Maya Chen: target type = ip, pods on CNI. sample from tonight:
```
type:Request elb_status_code:504 target_status_code:504 target:10.0.64.23:8080 reason:connection_reset
```
Tom Alvarez: saw conntrack and SNAT port exhaustion on a few nodes earlier today during the burst. autoscaler brought up 24 nodes -> lots more pods -> egress ephemeral ports thrashed. ALB healthcheck TCP->HTTP probes were getting RSTs.
Jared Kahn: that would explain it. if NAT port allocation stalls we’ll get half-open connections. cloudwatch for the nat gw shows SourcePortAllocationLimit reached in one AZ.
cloudwatch-bot: ALERT: NATGateway Port Allocation High (us-west-2a) — 97% used over 3m. https://console.aws.amazon.com/cloudwatch/alerts/ID
Lin Wei: extra twist: these are GPU nodes. device plugin initialization delays readiness for pods that mount GPUs. pods are Created but not Ready for several seconds while kernel modules/drivers load. combined with egress port pressure healthchecks time out.
Maya Chen: so two simultaneous issues: (1) GPU readiness lag extends window where pod responds slowly to probes; (2) egress port scarcity causes probes to fail even if pod is responding. both cause ALB to mark unhealthy.
Tom Alvarez: quick mitigation: increase target group's healthy threshold + lower unhealthy threshold? we can also lengthen health check timeout from 5s -> 10s for edge TG. low-effort.
Jared Kahn: mitigation options:
- increase NAT capacity (additional NAT GW per AZ or scale managed NAT) 
- move probes to hostNetwork or use node-local health proxy so probes bypass SNAT
- enable VPC CNI warm IP target or use AWS VPC CNI EKS pod ENI (assign ips) 
- change TG to instance targets (but we lose pod-level granularity)
- bump healthcheck interval/timeout
Lin Wei: hostNetwork for the probe is attractive: kubelet/nodeTCP will avoid SNAT. but we need to be careful with port collisions. alternative is use node-local sidecar that responds on node loopback.
Maya Chen: cost note: adding NAT GW per AZ adds ~$x00/mo/az. customers will see cost creep if we replicate NAT per nodepool. need product to sign off if we propose that.
Tom Alvarez: short-term I can patch our helm chart to extend readinessProbe initialDelay and timeout for GPU pods and raise the TG timeout from 5->10s. that'll reduce churn during scale-ups. I'll open a PR.
Jared Kahn: I'll file a network ticket to request temporary extra NAT capacity for the affected AZ and ask infra procurement about long-term options (e.g., AWS PrivateLink NAT pool, or NAT Gateway scaling policy).
Lin Wei: also adding a 10s deregistration delay on the TG will prevent immediate evictions while node warms up. we should test effect with a dry run in staging.
Maya Chen: action items:
- Tom: PR to bump readiness/init delays + TG timeout change (staging first)
- Jared: net ticket + cost estimate for extra NAT GW per-az or managed service
- Lin: run a scale-up in staging with enhanced logging and tcpdump on node to reproduce probe RSTs
cloudwatch-bot: NOTE: Alert acknowledged by Jared Kahn at 2019998975
Tom Alvarez: noted. will push the helm patch in ~30m and kick off a staging scale test. :rocket:
Maya Chen: thanks team. will keep this thread updated with results.
